routing.guard_desc: After SkyrimNet sends a request, a model can sit silent for a while before its first word arrives. These settings decide how long SkyrimNet waits for that first word before it stops waiting and hands the request to the next model in your rotation. The wait is sized from how quickly the other models have been starting their answers, so a setup full of fast providers gives up sooner than one built on slow ones. The defaults suit most setups.
routing.guard_early_abort: Give up on a slow first word
routing.guard_early_abort_hint: On: when a model has not started answering by the deadline, SkyrimNet abandons that attempt and sends the request to the next model. Off: every attempt waits the full request timeout, however long the model stays silent. The race, minimum wait and cold-start wait then do nothing; the patience multiplier still drives the demotion at the bottom.
routing.guard_race: Keep the abandoned attempt in the race
routing.guard_race_hint: On: the abandoned attempt keeps running in the background while the next model is tried, and whichever one starts answering first is the one you hear. Off: the abandoned attempt is only timed for the statistics, and anything it eventually says is thrown away.
routing.guard_multiplier_hint: How much longer a model may take to start answering than the best alternative usually needs. At 2, a model gets twice the time the next-best option would need before SkyrimNet gives up on it. Lower is stricter, higher is more forgiving (1.5–10, default 2). The same ratio decides when a provider counts as slow for the demotion below, so it stays in effect even with the give-up switch off.
routing.guard_floor_hint: The deadline never drops below this, however fast the alternatives are, so a brief network hiccup cannot make SkyrimNet abandon a healthy model (1000–10000, default 2500).
routing.guard_ceiling_hint: Used only while SkyrimNet has not yet seen how fast any model starts answering, typically the first request after launch. It is never shorter than the minimum wait above (3000–120000, default 15000). 0 turns it off, so that first request waits the full timeout.
routing.guard_slow_demote_hint: When a provider keeps starting its answers much later than the fastest one you have used this session (later by more than the patience multiplier), it is moved to the back of the line until you restart. It is still used when the others fail; it is just tried last.
